entries.ambiguity: Language, compiler platform, and execution ecosystem can be confused when downstream work names runtime behavior as language semantics.
entries.resolution: D0 separates the identities and requires artifacts to connect them; D3 rejects runtime/backend and profile/target conflation.

entries.ambiguity: Performance work can appear to justify erasing safety checks without retained or regenerated evidence.
entries.resolution: D6, D8, and D9 are bound by the safety-performance gate model; a pass must preserve, regenerate, retain, or reject.

entries.ambiguity: Profile legality can be moved after target lowering if profile and target are treated as the same concept.
entries.resolution: The terminology registry rejects profile/target conflation and the milestone evidence system blocks deferred safety or profile legality claims.

entries.ambiguity: A file path can be mistaken for artifact identity when provenance is not recorded.
entries.resolution: The terminology registry requires artifact identity fields and the milestone evidence system requires emitted artifacts and provenance records.

entries.ambiguity: Self-hosting progress can be mistaken for permission to retire seed compiler trust before equivalence evidence exists.
entries.resolution: The change-control workflow requires bootstrap equivalence evidence before bootstrap trust changes are accepted.
